world_org_meetings.title: Turkey: Delegates arrive in Antalya as COP31 climate talks begin
world_org_meetings.description: The United Nations COP31 climate summit has opened in Antalya after a year marked by deadly heatwaves and devastating floods. Delegates face fresh challenges as the war in Iran disrupts global energy supplies.

world_org_meetings.title: Philippines: 'Trump out!' Women rally ahead of ASEAN summit
world_org_meetings.description: Women protesters took to the streets of Manila on Monday 9 November ahead of Donald Trump's visit for the 49th ASEAN summit. Carrying "Trump Out" placards, they also denounced a US-led initiative on semiconductors and critical minerals.

world_org_meetings.title: All eyes on Rubio as Iran, Ukraine set to dominate G7 meeting in Paris
world_org_meetings.description: G7 foreign ministers began two days of talks in Paris on Monday as they grapple with multiple unresolved global crises. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is likely to face questions about whether the Trump administration will shift its positions on the conflicts in Ukraine and Iran in particular following the Democrats sweeping victory in the midterms. France 24’s Clovis Casali has more.

world_org_meetings.title: COP31: A focus on electrification as extreme weather events shake the world
world_org_meetings.description: Most of the world’s countries are gathering this week for COP31 in Antalya, Turkey. This United Nations Climate Change Conference opens amid deep concern following extreme weather events such as the deadly floods in Nepal and a supersized El Niño. Experts say that in uncertain times, it is even more important to accelerate global efforts.

world_org_meetings.title: UK and EU agree draft deal to scrap Brexit red tape over food exports
world_org_meetings.description: The food deal, ahead of a UK-EU summit later this month, is the most significant part of the so-called Brexit reset agreed so far.

diplomatic_visits.title: Argentina: Pope Leo XIV welcomed by Javier Milei for historic visit
diplomatic_visits.description: Pope Leo XIV has arrived in Argentina, on Sunday 8 November, for the first papal visit to the country in nearly 40 years. President Javier Milei welcomed him at Buenos Aires airport, while the city's iconic obelisk was illuminated in his honour.

diplomatic_visits.title: Qatar PM meets with Trump for talks on ending war on Iran
diplomatic_visits.description: Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani has met with US President Donald Trump.

diplomatic_visits.title: Pope visits struggling Argentine home for people with disabilities to press message
diplomatic_visits.description: Pope Leo XIV has renewed his call for Argentina to protect its most vulnerable people, visiting a home for people with disabilities in a symbolically powerful rebuke of President Javier Milei’s austerity measures

diplomatic_visits.title: Pope wraps up Uruguay visit and heads to most fraught stop of his tour in Argentina
diplomatic_visits.description: Pope Leo XIV has delivered a diplomatic but subtly strong critique of Argentine President Javier Milei’s austerity measures and libertarian agenda

diplomatic_visits.title: 'A tricky day' ahead for French PM as he meets with unions amid social unrest
diplomatic_visits.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu is to meet unions and employer federation representatives on Monday to discuss salaries and purchasing power following a wave of social unrest across France in recent weeks. But, says France 24's Rochelle Ferguson, he faces a tricky task if his is to meet unions' wage demands and take steps towards placating widespread public anger.

elections.title: Republican congressman to force impeachment vote on Defence Secretary Hegseth
elections.description: The effort will likely fail, but Representative Thomas Massie wants to push Trump to fire Hegseth before Democrats can launch their own impeachment process next year.

elections.title: South Africa’s ANC suffers a historic setback in local elections as coalition talks begin
elections.description: South Africa’s ruling ANC suffers its worst-ever local election results, securing just 30% of the vote, as coalition talks loom. Meanwhile, former Ugandan military intelligence officer Herbert Matanda Mabonga accuses the army of secretly detaining and torturing opponents, following the release of videos that sparked national outrage. Finally, in Senegal, more than 200,000 free tickets are giving young people the chance to experience the games live on home soil, in a bid to inspire a new generation of athletes.

elections.title: French Judo superstar Teddy Riner says will run for president
elections.description: France's multiple Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner announced on Monday he would run in next year's presidential election, after expressing concern about the "rise of the far right". "My name is Teddy Riner and today, I am telling you face to face: I am a candidate in the 2027 presidential election," the 37-year-old said in a surprise announcement on social media. Riner, one of the greatest judokas in history, said in the two-minute-37-second video that he feared France could soon become deeply divided, appearing to cast himself as a candidate for voters unwilling to choose between two political extremes -- the far right and the hard left. FRANCE 24's Mark Owen speaks with Yves Sintomer, Professor of Political Science at Université Paris VIII.

elections.title: Social unrest ahead of French elections: Protesters 'don't believe politics can achieve anything'
elections.description: Annette Young is pleased to welcome Renaud Foucart, Senior Lecturer at the Department of Economics ECARES at Lancaster University. France's 1.6% minimum-wage increase, in response to the countrywide protests, may offer a temporary reprieve from social unrest, but it does little to resolve the deeper political and institutional crisis confronting the country. According to Foucart, the central problem extends beyond declining purchasing power, fiscal constraints and the limitations of a minority government. It concerns a growing loss of faith in politics itself. “They are in the street because they don't believe politics can achieve anything,” Foucart argues, suggesting that the persistence of mass demonstrations ahead of the presidential election reflects profound disillusionment with the political system's capacity to deliver meaningful change.

elections.title: Trump reverses stance, alleges fraud in recent US midterm elections
elections.description: Democratic Senate leader Schumer criticises Trump's poll denialism, calling it an avoidable return to baseless claims.
